headline: Volcanoes are Earth's pressure valves—releasing energy from deep below
universal_truth: Pressure that isn't released will eventually find its own way out
fun_facts: Lava temperature ranges from 1,300°F to 2,200°F—hot enough to melt steel
There are about 1,500 active volcanoes on Earth; about 50 erupt each year
Volcanic eruptions have caused mass extinctions but also created fertile soil and new land
discussion_questions: What pressures in your life need healthy release?
How can destruction also be creation?
What would Earth be like without volcanoes?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Beneath your feet, Earth is molten. The planet's interior is so hot that rock flows like thick honey. Occasionally, this liquid rock finds a path to the surface—and a volcano is born. Today, we descend into Earth's fiery depths.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Why does rock melt deep underground? And why does it sometimes explode to the surface violently, while other times it oozes gently? What determines whether a volcano whispers or screams?
cliff.prompt: What makes some volcanic eruptions explosive?

options.text: High silica content makes magma thick and traps gas until pressure explodes
options.response: Exactly. Thick, sticky magma holds gas until it bursts violently. Thin magma lets gas escape gently.

options.text: The deeper the magma chamber, the more violent the eruption
options.response: Depth matters, but the key factor is magma composition...

q1.title: Melting Earth
q1.script: Earth's mantle isn't entirely liquid—it's mostly solid rock that flows very slowly over millions of years. But where tectonic plates pull apart or push together, rock melts into magma. This molten rock rises because it's less dense than solid rock around it.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Melting Earth"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Pressure Valves
q2.script: Think of volcanoes as pressure release valves. Without them, Earth's internal heat would build catastrophically. Volcanoes let the planet breathe, releasing pressure gradually—usually. When the system clogs, explosions follow.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Creation Through Destruction
q3.script: Volcanic eruptions devastate landscapes—but they also create. Hawaii was built entirely by volcanoes. Volcanic ash becomes incredibly fertile soil. Over time, what seems like destruction becomes the foundation for new life.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Pressure needs release. Emotions, stress, creative energy—if not expressed, they build until they erupt. Find healthy vents for what's building inside. Controlled release beats catastrophic explosion.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 52. Tomorrow, we'll discover why the ground shakes. Until then, appreciate that you're walking on a thin crust over a molten world.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Pressure Release - Find Your Vents
growTrack.learning_objective: Identify healthy outlets for life's pressures
growTrack.activity: What pressure is building in your life right now—stress, frustration, unexpressed creativity? Identify one healthy 'vent'—exercise, conversation, creative work, rest. Use it today before pressure finds its own way out.
